newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt says can function despite sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt says can function despite sex scandal.

text.p: The Belgian government said on Tuesday it was still able to function despite the fact that a senior minister is under investigation over allegations that he had sex with minors.

"The Belgian government is continuing its work normally, it has proved before that it is able to do this under difficult circumstances," Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's spokeswoman told Reuters.
Parliament will set up a special commission later this afternoon to study the allegations against Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo.

Belgian financial markets have kept a close eye on the new scandal -- another one in a long series of financial, sex and murder scandals that have haunted the Dehaene government -- but the damage so far is limited mainly to a slight weakening of the Belgian franc.
At 1345 GMT the franc was quoted 20.6105/25 to the mark, slightly firmer than Monday's 20.6140/60 three-month low.
Belgian linear bonds' yield premium over equivalent German bunds stood at 17 basis points in midday trade, virtually unchanged from Monday and last week.
